result.scope: Static behavior investigation of POST /api/v1/retrieval/process/file, its file lookups and updates, and save_docs_to_vector_db in open-webui/open-webui@841c9045d789005145274955e7ef60b1b11a9be9.

answers.explanation: The route requires get_verified_user, which accepts role user or admin. It authorizes the input file differently by role: admin uses an ID-only lookup, while a non-admin lookup requires both the supplied file_id and user.id; failure produces 404. Once a file is selected, the handler updates that file row by file.id. The vector destination is not necessarily the authorized file object: a supplied collection_name is retained as an independent destination, while only a missing (None) collection_name is derived as file-{file.id}. With embedding enabled, the supplied destination is passed to save_docs_to_vector_db with add=true. That helper queries/checks/inserts by collection name but performs no visible caller or collection-owner lookup. Therefore a regular caller with an owned input file can direct its content into another named collection if that name is accepted by the backend; the route does not establish ownership of that destination. A regular caller cannot process another user's file because the owner-filtered lookup returns no file, whereas an admin can process any file found by id. If BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is true, the selected file is updated but no vector write occurs. The source also shows nuanced data paths: supplied content first attempts to delete the selected file's default file-{id} collection; with a destination but no content, documents are copied from the default file collection or stored file data. Remaining limits are static-analysis only: runtime middleware, vector-backend tenant isolation, collection-name acceptance/secrecy, and deployment configuration were not observed. The semantic checker also retains unresolved class-receiver/call-link bindings, so its two role paths remain formally unknown even though the directly read source establishes the predicates described above.
